exercises.en: The people who live in our neighborhood are kind.
exercises.why: Present ~는 on an ㄹ-stem drops the ㄹ: 살다 → 사는.

exercises.en: The apples I bought at the market yesterday are really delicious.
exercises.why: A finished action uses the past modifier ~ㄴ after a vowel stem.

exercises.en: I bought clothes that I will wear next week.
exercises.why: A future action uses ~을 after a consonant stem.

exercises.en: I like making Korean food.
exercises.why: ~는 것 turns the action into a noun, and 만들다 drops ㄹ before ~는.

exercises.en: Exercising in the morning is good.
exercises.why: 것 ends in a consonant and is the subject of the adjective 좋다, so it takes 이.

exercises.en: Today I ate the food that was left over yesterday.
exercises.why: Past modifier ~은 goes after a consonant stem like 남-.

exercises.ko: 허리를 ___ 선수는 오늘 경기를 안 해요.
exercises.en: The player who hurt his back isn't playing in today's game.
exercises.why: The injury already happened, so use the past modifier ~ㄴ.

exercises.en: I have a question that I will ask tomorrow.
exercises.why: For a future action, a vowel stem takes ~ㄹ.

exercises.en: I don't like cleaning.
The neighborhood I live in is clean.
I have a lot of things to do tomorrow.
Do you know the man who is talking with that older woman?

reading.ko: 우리 동네에는 작은 가게가 있어요. 가게에서 일하는 아줌마는 아주 친절해요. 저는 그 가게에서 물건을 사는 것을 좋아해요. 어제 산 사과는 정말 맛있었어요. 오늘은 친구에게 줄 과일을 샀어요. 내일 친구와 같이 먹을 거예요.
reading.en: There is a small shop in our neighborhood. The older woman who works at the shop is very kind. I like buying things at that shop. The apples I bought yesterday were really delicious. Today I bought fruit to give to my friend. Tomorrow I will eat it together with my friend.

exercises.en: Where is the spoon I used to use every day?
exercises.why: ~던 attaches straight to the stem for something done repeatedly in the past.

exercises.ko: 제가 한때 자주 ___ 공원에 오늘 다시 갔어요.
exercises.en: Today I went again to the park I once used to go to often.
exercises.why: Repeated past habit: stem + ~던.

exercises.ko: 작년에 한 번 ___ 식당에 다시 가고 싶어요.
exercises.en: I want to go again to the restaurant I went to once last year.
exercises.why: A one-time, finished action takes ~았/었던, and 가 + 았 contracts to 갔.

exercises.ko: 한때 ___ 우리 동네가 지금은 아주 깨끗해요.
exercises.en: Our neighborhood, which was once dirty, is very clean now.
exercises.why: A past state of an adjective takes ~았/었던, and 더럽다 is ㅂ-irregular.

exercises.en: Even the time I was lonely in Korea is precious to me.
exercises.why: 외롭다 is ㅂ-irregular: 외로워 + ㅆ던 for a past state.

exercises.en: Who ate the hamburger I was eating?
exercises.why: ~던 shows the eating was in progress and not finished.

exercises.ko: 제가 오 년 동안 ___ 회사가 문을 닫았어요.
exercises.en: The company I had worked at for five years closed down.
exercises.why: 하다 + 였 becomes 했, then add ~던.

exercises.en: The juice that shop used to sell was really delicious.
exercises.why: ㄹ-stems keep their ㄹ before ~던.

exercises.en: This is the calendar I used last year.
The pharmacy I used to go to often is next to the post office.
exercises.ko: 제가 자주 가던 약국은 우체국 옆에 있어요.

exercises.en: The movie I saw last year was really fun.
My friend, who was once lonely, is happy now.
exercises.ko: 한때 외로웠던 제 친구는 지금 행복해요.

reading.ko: 우리 동네에 제가 자주 가던 식당이 있었어요. 그 식당의 햄버거는 정말 맛있었어요. 종업원들도 아주 친절했어요. 하지만 작년에 그 식당이 문을 닫았어요. 어제 그 식당이 있던 곳에 갔어요. 지금 거기에는 약국이 있어요. 저는 그 식당에서 먹었던 햄버거를 영원히 잊지 않을 거예요.
reading.en: There was a restaurant in our neighborhood that I used to go to often. That restaurant's hamburgers were really delicious. The servers were very kind too. But last year that restaurant closed. Yesterday I went to the place where the restaurant used to be. Now there is a pharmacy there. I will never forget the hamburgers I ate at that restaurant.

exercises.en: Is the cake I made tasty?
exercises.why: An ㄹ-stem drops ㄹ and takes ~ㄴ for the past: 만들다 → 만든.

exercises.en: The music I listened to yesterday was really good.
exercises.why: 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before ~은.

exercises.en: The neighbor who helped me was really kind.
exercises.why: 돕다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우, then ~ㄴ.

exercises.en: The house my friend built is very big.
exercises.why: 짓다 is ㅅ-irregular: ㅅ drops but the stem still takes ~은.

exercises.en: My favorite sport is volleyball.
exercises.why: "Favorite" is 가장/제일 좋아하는 + noun.

exercises.en: My favorite season is autumn.
exercises.why: The speaker is the subject of 좋아하다 inside the clause, so use 제가, not 저의.

exercises.ko: 제가 살고 ___ 곳은 바다가 가까운 곳이에요.
exercises.en: The place I want to live is somewhere near the sea.
exercises.why: 싶다 is an adjective, so it takes ~은 to describe a noun.

exercises.en: There is a lot of delicious fruit on this farm.
exercises.why: Words built on 있다/없다 take ~는, even though they are adjectives.

exercises.en: My favorite food is kimchi stew.
That person I met yesterday was really honest.
exercises.ko: 제가 어제 만난 그 사람은 정말 솔직했어요.

exercises.en: The country I want to go to is Korea.
The story I heard yesterday was interesting.

reading.ko: 제가 제일 좋아하는 운동은 농구예요. 제 친구 민수가 제일 좋아하는 운동은 배구예요. 우리는 주말마다 같이 운동해요. 지난주에는 민수가 만든 김밥을 먹었어요. 정말 맛있었어요. 다음 주말에는 제가 가고 싶은 농장에 같이 갈 거예요. 거기에는 재미있는 동물이 많아요.
reading.en: My favorite sport is basketball. My friend Minsu's favorite sport is volleyball. We exercise together every weekend. Last week I ate the gimbap Minsu made. It was really delicious. Next weekend we will go together to a farm I want to visit. There are lots of fun animals there.

questions.q: 이 사람이 제일 좋아하는 운동은 뭐예요?

exercises.en: Parking is hard in this neighborhood.
exercises.why: Stem + ~기 makes a noun, often used with 어렵다, 쉽다 and 좋다.

exercises.en: The child suddenly started to cry.
exercises.why: "Start doing" is stem + ~기 시작하다; ㄹ stays before ~기.

exercises.en: I started exercising last month.
exercises.why: The tense goes on 시작하다, and last month needs the past.

exercises.en: I don't want to do anything today.
exercises.why: "Not want to" is stem + ~기 싫다.

exercises.en: My younger sibling doesn't want to do homework.
exercises.why: For someone other than the speaker, use ~기 싫어하다.

exercises.en: I often have fights with my older brother.
exercises.why: 싸우다 ends in a vowel, so it takes ~ㅁ to become the noun 싸움.

exercises.en: Our child is our great joy.
exercises.why: 기쁘다 ends in a vowel, so add ~ㅁ: 기쁨.

exercises.en: Tomorrow's to-dos are doing homework and exercising.
exercises.why: To-do lists use the short noun form stem + ~기.

exercises.en: Korean is hard to pronounce.
It started to snow.
I don't want to get up early tomorrow.
My friend and I had a fight yesterday.

reading.ko: 저는 작년에 한국어를 공부하기 시작했어요. 한국어는 읽기는 쉬워요. 하지만 말하기는 어려워요. 저는 매일 한국 친구와 이야기해요. 친구의 도움은 저에게 아주 소중해요. 오늘은 공부하기 싫어요. 하지만 내일 시험이 있어요.
reading.en: I started studying Korean last year. Reading Korean is easy. But speaking is hard. I talk with a Korean friend every day. My friend's help is very precious to me. Today I don't want to study. But I have a test tomorrow.

questions.q: 이 사람은 언제 한국어를 공부하기 시작했어요?

exercises.en: Do you know what time the bus comes?
exercises.why: For an embedded question, attach ~는지 to a verb stem with no space.

exercises.en: I don't know how heavy this bag is.
exercises.why: Adjectives take ~ㄴ/은지, and 무겁다 is ㅂ-irregular.

exercises.en: I don't know why my friend cried yesterday.
exercises.why: For the past, use ~았/었는지.

exercises.en: I asked where the exit is.
exercises.why: 이다 always becomes ~인지.

exercises.ko: 그 식당이 오늘 문을 여는지 안 ___ 몰라요.
exercises.en: I don't know whether that restaurant is open today or not.
exercises.why: Repeat the clause after 안 for "whether or not"; 열다 drops ㄹ before ~는지.

exercises.en: It might be chilly tomorrow.
exercises.why: "Might" is ~ㄹ/을지도 모르다.

exercises.en: It has been three months since I started my part-time job.
exercises.why: "It has been X since" uses the past modifier ~ㄴ/은 + 지.

exercises.en: I have been living in Seoul for two years.
exercises.why: 살다 drops ㄹ and takes ~ㄴ before 지.

exercises.en: I don't know where the post office is.
It might snow tomorrow.
How long has it been since you came to Korea?
I don't know whether my friend will come or not.

reading.ko: 저는 서울에 산 지 일 년 됐어요. 서울은 지하철이 아주 편해요. 하지만 처음에는 몇 호선을 타는지 몰랐어요. 그때 역에서 일하는 사람에게 물어봤어요. 오늘은 친구를 만나요. 그런데 친구가 몇 번 출구에 있는지 몰라요. 친구에게 전화할 거예요.
reading.en: It has been a year since I started living in Seoul. The subway in Seoul is very convenient. But at first I didn't know which line to take. Back then I asked a person who works at the station. Today I'm meeting a friend. But I don't know which exit my friend is at. I will call my friend.

questions.q: 이 사람은 서울에 산 지 얼마나 됐어요?

exercises.en: My friend, who is a doctor, is always busy.
exercises.why: 이다 takes ~ㄴ to describe a noun: N1인 N2.

exercises.en: My younger sibling, who is a student, gets an allowance.
exercises.why: N인 + noun works after both vowels and consonants.

exercises.en: I don't know what that building is.
exercises.why: 이다 + ~ㄴ지 is always 인지, written without a space.

exercises.en: I forgot that tomorrow is my sibling's birthday.
exercises.why: "The fact that X is Y" is N인 것.

exercises.en: Did you know that person is a singer?
exercises.why: The clause is the object of 알다, so 것 takes 을.

exercises.en: That person did something illegal.
exercises.why: 불법 is a noun, so it describes 일 with 인.

exercises.en: I don't know how much this necklace is.
exercises.why: After a noun or question word like 얼마, use 인지.

exercises.en: I envy my friend who is rich.
exercises.why: Noun + 인 describes the next noun.

exercises.en: My friend, who is a nurse, works at a hospital.
Do you know what day it is today?
I didn't know that person was a student.
I have a friend who is the same age as me.

reading.ko: 제 친구 지민은 의사예요. 의사인 지민은 항상 바빠요. 지민과 저는 동갑이에요. 어제는 지민의 생일이었어요. 그런데 저는 어제가 지민의 생일인 것을 몰랐어요. 오늘 지민에게 줄 목걸이를 샀어요. 이 목걸이가 지민에게 어울리는지 모르겠어요.
reading.en: My friend Jimin is a doctor. Jimin, who is a doctor, is always busy. Jimin and I are the same age. Yesterday was Jimin's birthday. But I didn't know yesterday was Jimin's birthday. Today I bought a necklace to give to Jimin. I'm not sure whether this necklace suits Jimin.

exercises.en: I bought vegetables to make gimbap.
exercises.why: ㄹ-stems take ~려고; ~러 is only used with movement verbs.

exercises.en: I turned on the light to read a book.
exercises.why: A consonant stem takes ~으려고; 켜다 is not a movement verb, so not ~으러.

exercises.en: I went out to eat lunch.
exercises.why: Before a movement verb, a consonant stem takes ~으러.

exercises.en: I went to the department store to buy clothes.
exercises.why: A vowel stem takes ~러 before 가다.

exercises.en: I plan to clean the house this weekend.
exercises.why: ~(으)려고 하다 means "plan to / intend to".

exercises.en: I try hard to speak in Korean every day.
exercises.why: ~(으)려고 노력하다 means "try hard to".

exercises.en: Yesterday I tried making kimchi for the first time.
exercises.why: "Try doing" is verb + ~아/어 보다.

exercises.en: I have never been on a plane.
exercises.why: Experience uses the past modifier: ~아/어 본 적이 있다/없다.

exercises.en: I came to Korea to study.
Have you ever eaten kimchi?
I'm going to a restaurant to meet a friend.
I plan to apply for that job.

reading.ko: 저는 요즘 일자리를 구하고 있어요. 어제는 이력서를 쓰려고 도서관에 갔어요. 저는 이력서를 써 본 적이 없어요. 이력서를 쓰는 것은 정말 어려웠어요. 오늘은 친구를 만나러 친구 집에 갔어요. 친구는 비서로 일한 적이 있어요. 우리는 같이 이력서를 다시 썼어요.
reading.en: These days I'm looking for a job. Yesterday I went to the library to write a resume. I have never written a resume. Writing a resume was really hard. Today I went to my friend's house to meet my friend. My friend has worked as a secretary before. We rewrote the resume together.

questions.q: 이 사람은 전에 이력서를 써 본 적이 있어요?
친구는 무슨 일을 한 적이 있어요?

exercises.en: I'm in the middle of doing homework right now.
exercises.why: "In the middle of" is stem + ~는 중이다.

exercises.en: That shopping building is under construction now.
exercises.why: 중 attaches straight to 하다-nouns like 공사.

exercises.en: While my friend showered, I ate breakfast.
exercises.why: "While" is stem + ~는 동안.

exercises.en: While living in Seoul, I took the subway every day.
exercises.why: ~는 동안 with 살다: ㄹ drops before ~는.

exercises.en: Between coffee and juice, which do you like more?
exercises.why: N 중에 means "among / between" when choosing.

exercises.ko: 제가 가 본 나라 ___ 한국이 제일 좋았어요.
exercises.en: Of the countries I have been to, I liked Korea the most.
exercises.why: A described noun + 중에 means "of / among".

exercises.en: I will move sometime next month.
exercises.why: Time + 중으로 means "sometime within that time".

exercises.en: Yesterday evening I was in the middle of watching a movie.
exercises.why: Keep ~는 and put the past tense on 이다: 중이었어요.

exercises.en: I'm in the middle of editing a photo.
I read a book while waiting for the bus.
Among these, which one is the cheapest?
I will finish my homework sometime today.

reading.ko: 저는 교환학생이에요. 이번 학기 동안 서울에서 공부하고 있어요. 지금은 도서관에서 강의 자료를 정리하는 중이에요. 제가 듣는 강의 중에 한국 지리 강의가 제일 재미있어요. 다음 주에 시험이 있어요. 이번 주 중으로 숙제를 끝낼 거예요.
reading.en: I am an exchange student. I'm studying in Seoul during this semester. Right now I'm in the library organizing lecture materials. Of the lectures I take, the Korean geography lecture is the most interesting. There is a test next week. I will finish my homework sometime this week.

questions.q: 이 사람은 지금 뭐 하는 중이에요?
